# Delirium Family Guide

> The website for the book "Delirium (Acute Confusion): A Family Guide to Sudden Changes in Thinking and Memory", by Professor Alasdair MacLullich and Dr Sharmella Summan, published by Delirium Support Press. The Kindle edition is planned for the end of October 2026, with paperback and hardback planned for the same time or soon after.

Delirium is a sudden change in thinking and attention, usually triggered by illness, surgery or medicines. It affects about one in four older people in hospital, yet many families have never heard of it. The book is written in plain English for people who have had delirium and for families and carers. It explains what delirium is, what families might see, how clinical teams assess and treat its causes, how relatives and carers can help, and what recovery can be like. It includes advice for people living with dementia, and Dr Summan's account of her own delirium as a patient in intensive care. It has 31 chapters in six sections.

Alasdair MacLullich is Professor of Geriatric Medicine at the University of Edinburgh and a consultant physician at the Royal Infirmary of Edinburgh. He created the 4AT, a delirium test used in hospitals worldwide, and co-chaired the Scottish national guideline on delirium (SIGN 157, 2019). Profiles: https://www.alasdairmaclullich.com/, https://orcid.org/0000-0003-3159-9370, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alasdair_MacLullich, https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q48288045. Sharmella Summan is a doctor who has worked in hospitals and general practice and now works in a hospice; she has also had delirium as a patient.

Facts:
- Title: Delirium (Acute Confusion): A Family Guide to Sudden Changes in Thinking and Memory
- Authors: Alasdair MacLullich and Sharmella Summan
- Publisher: Delirium Support Press
- ISBN, paperback: 978-1-918164-01-5
- ISBN, hardback: 978-1-918164-02-2
- Free sample: Chapter 1 as an illustrated PDF, sent by email: https://deliriumfamilyguide.com/#free-chapter
- Anyone worried about sudden confusion now should seek prompt medical assessment: https://deliriumsupport.com/get-help-now/

## Pages

- [Home](https://deliriumfamilyguide.com/): about the book, four questions families ask with short answers, the first page, the full contents, the authors and publication details
- [Chapter 1: Understanding delirium](https://deliriumfamilyguide.com/chapter-1/): the opening pages of Chapter 1, word for word from the book
- [In their words](https://deliriumfamilyguide.com/voices/): 25 quotations from patients and families about delirium, each copied word for word from a published account and linked to its source
- [Medical and editorial policy](https://deliriumfamilyguide.com/editorial.html): authorship, sources for figures, how quotations are checked, corrections

## Related websites by the same author

- [Delirium Support](https://deliriumsupport.com/): free information about delirium in plain English for patients, families and carers
- [The 4AT](https://www.the4at.com/): the 4AT delirium assessment test, for healthcare staff
- [Delirium Academy](https://deliriumacademy.com/): free delirium courses for healthcare staff
- [Delirium, dementia and better care](https://alasdairmaclullich.substack.com/): Alasdair MacLullich's free newsletter on Substack
- [Alasdair MacLullich](https://www.alasdairmaclullich.com/): the author's professional website
